```plato
//==
// # Collision
//
// Narrow-phase bodies for `collision.types.plato`: the primitive pair tests that
// produce contact points, the manifold that groups them for a body pair, and the
// flattening into the constraint rows `rigid-dynamics.library.plato` solves.
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Material combination
//  - Contact frames
//  - Primitive pair tests
//  - Manifolds
//  - Constraint rows
//  - Warm starting
//
// CONVENTIONS THAT GOVERN EVERY PAIR TEST HERE, stated once:
//
//   * THE NORMAL POINTS FROM A TOWARD B, where A is the FIRST parameter — the
//     invariant `collision.types.plato` already states for `ContactPoint3D`. The
//     solver reads it as "an impulse of +P along the normal is applied to B and
//     -P to A", so a ball resting on a ground plane, tested as
//     `Collide(ball, ground)`, gets a normal pointing DOWN and is pushed UP.
//     Swapping the arguments of a pair test therefore changes the sign of the
//     result and is not the same call.
//   * PENETRATION IS POSITIVE WHEN THE SHAPES OVERLAP, and is the depth along the
//     normal. Zero is exact touching.
//   * AN EMPTY POINT ARRAY MEANS "NOT TOUCHING". No hit flag and no sentinel: an
//     empty array is this vocabulary's own encoding of "none"
//     (CONVENTIONS.md - Typed indices), and it is also the honest shape for a
//     test like box-versus-plane whose answer is naturally several points.
//   * THE CONTACT POSITION SITS ON THE B-SIDE SURFACE where the two disagree,
//     because that is the surface a penetration is measured back from. The
//     difference is at most the penetration depth and is invisible for shallow
//     contacts, which is the regime a solver is meant to stay in.

library Collision
{
    //==
    // # Material combination
    //
    // Two touching bodies each carry their own friction and restitution; a
    // contact needs one number for each. `PhysicsMaterial` says which rule to
    // apply, per coefficient, and the two materials' rules may disagree — so the
    // pair needs a rule as well as two values. The rule taken is A's: a contact is
    // asked for by one of the two, and letting the FIRST material decide is the
    // only choice that does not need a tie-break rule of its own.

    // The two coefficients merged under one combine rule.
    Combine(kind: MaterialCombine, a: Number, b: Number): Number
        => match (kind) {
            Average => (a + b) * 0.5;
            Min => a.Min(b);
            Max => a.Max(b);
            Multiply => a * b;
        };
```
